name: Orthodontist

google_prefill.phone: [G] the listed phone (stays the business's; customers use Rosie's one number)

A.flow: A: the customer comes to the business (video or phone count as A)

services.name: New patient check with X-rays
services.story: The main story: a $35 new patient check with X-rays. Nothing is taken. The desk checks Alex's plan, and Alex pays the share at the front desk.

services.name: New patient check with X-rays
services.story: The same check where the office turns on its $20 missed-visit fee. A card is saved for it, never for a fee-free patient.

services.name: Braces or clear aligners (full treatment)
services.story: Braces or clear aligners, $5,500 in all: a $500 deposit when starting, and the $5,000 rest paid at the front desk over the visits.

services.name: Braces check and retainer fitting
services.story: A $55 braces check and retainer fitting, paid in full when booked. Nothing more is owed after.

services.name: Retainer repair, quoted from photos
services.story: A retainer repair quoted from Alex's photos at $90. A $20 deposit once the quote is OK'd, and the $70 rest at the visit.

services.name: Bracket repair
services.story: A broken bracket the same day. Only the $25 check is promised; any repair is priced first, with Alex's yes.

B.flow: B: the business goes to the customer
B.staff: Priya (orthodontist) and Ben (orthodontic assistant), who travel with a portable kit
B.customer: Alex M. (patient, lives at Riverside care home) · other patients

services.name: Braces check at a care home
services.story: The main story: a $179 braces check at Riverside care home. Nothing is taken. The office bills Alex's plan its own way.

services.name: Braces check at a care home
services.story: The same check, paid privately: nothing is taken when booking, and Rosie texts the bill when Priya texts DONE.

services.name: Broken bracket at a care home
services.story: A broken bracket at the care home. Only the $89 visit fee is promised; the repair is priced at the visit, with Alex's yes first.

services.name: New retainer, quoted from the scan
services.story: A new retainer, quoted by Priya from photos of the care-home scan at $640. A $160 deposit when the quote is OK'd, and Rosie texts the bill for the $480 rest.

services_shape: visit types in a chair, each with a set length; a braces start is a bonding visit, then set adjustment visits; an emergency fix is booked the same day with the owner's OK; every visit needs a free chair
questions_before_times: for you, your child, or someone you help (a care home resident)
which visit: the office's own visit types only (a new patient check, braces, clear aligners, a retainer, or an emergency visit), never a symptom typed into the AI
a dental or orthodontic plan (its name only) or paying yourself
safety_stop: face or jaw swelling with a fever, or trouble breathing or swallowing
a tooth knocked loose or out, or bleeding that won't stop
swallowed something poisonous, or too much of a medicine
first_steps: Health history, consent and the plan's papers
A written price estimate for self-pay patients
A signed treatment agreement for braces or aligners
license: each orthodontist holds their own license from the state's dental board; an orthodontic assistant holds one only where the state licenses assistants
staff_skills: orthodontists: exams, braces, clear aligners, retainers and emergency fixes; orthodontic assistants: X-rays, photos, and the bracket and wire work the state allows; only people cleared for mobile visits go to care homes and schools
messages_never: texts carry only the practice's name, the date, the time, the address and a secure link: never the visit type, the plan, the reason, the results or the orthodontist's name (when the orthodontist comes to a care home, school or home, the name stays, for the door check); X-rays and photos never go through Rosie
demo_note: Demo data for testing only. [G] = prefilled from the business's Google listing at sign-up; the owner checks each field.
